text: The Alpha-1 Antitrypsin level is normal, which helps rule out that specific genetic cause. Given your hyperinflated lungs, obstruction, and the fact that symptoms worsen at night and with activity, do you have a history of significant exposure to dust, fumes, or chemical irritants at work or home?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I work as a landscaper, so I am frequently exposed to dust, pollen, and chemical fumes from the plants and maintenance products. I don't think I've ever worn a proper respirator mask while doing my daily work.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that clarification; your occupation as a landscaper with significant dust and chemical exposure strongly supports an environmental etiology. Have you noticed any specific seasonal worsening of symptoms, or do they persist regardless of the time of year?

REQUEST TEST: Methacholine Challenge Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your normal Methacholine challenge, the obstruction is likely not due to asthma, and your landscape work with dust exposure points toward chronic bronchitis. Do you currently smoke cigarettes or use other tobacco products?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I quit smoking about five years ago. I used to smoke half a pack a day for twenty years, but I haven't touched any tobacco since I stopped working in landscaping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis due to environmental exposure (occupational dust and chemical fumes).
